label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 2 uses a 7x7 board, 3 solution arrows, at most 4 placed arrows, 11 beats, and 300 ms between autonomous beats.
The full interface directly drags the visible brass seed arrow onto an empty square (cell_drag) and clicks a placed arrow to cycle its direction clockwise (cell_click).

Run 11 beats, step one beat, clear the configuration, revise after a completed film, and check the sequence are visible controls; checking is administrative after the outcome film. The configured observation bound is 600 ms over 5 chronological frames, with 120 seconds of play time.
autonomous_processes: Before a film starts, the edit phase is stationary: waiting does not move arrows or change the target, and full-mode placement/direction edits remain available.

RUN applies beat 1 synchronously in its handler, then schedules beats 2 through 11 with setTimeout at the 300 ms beat interval without further agent actions. Each beat moves open arrows, records a wall/slot event and reverses on a wall, or turns an arrow clockwise for an occupied or duplicate destination; the board and visible event ledger are rerendered.

Wall-hit slots flash autonomously and the flash CSS class is removed after up to 255 ms; this is presentation of the already-recorded event. After beat 11, the film changes to complete and enables later controls, but that fixed completion transition does not make an opportunity expire.
Manual STEP applies exactly one beat synchronously on the click; between step clicks there is no autonomous beat timer. Post-failure shake/flash cleanup is also presentation-only.

clause_i.reason: For the candidate full-edit mode across generated seeds, an action-history-only q cannot in general choose target-specific placements and directions: an initial edit history can be identical while the visible target wall ledger differs. This is only static observation dependence, not a real-time witness.

clause_ii.reason: The target wall/slot/beat ledger and current configuration are visible before the film, so a bounded screenshot window can choose the next full edit (even an endpoint frame is sufficient). The window does not need to predict a degrading action opportunity.

clause_iii.reason: The film is the only autonomous task-state evolution. During edit, waiting leaves every configuration choice equally effective. During the film, run and step are disabled, reset returns early, revise is disabled, and grid drops/clicks are rejected outside the edit phase, so no outcome-affecting action remains available while arrows and the ledger evolve. After completion, revise/check become available rather than expiring. Thus no legitimate grouped mode has an available action whose Q value or advantage strictly decreases from the visible non-clock evolution.

common_visible_process: The common visible process is the 11-beat, 300 ms film: arrows move, wall impacts reverse and flash wall slots, encounters turn arrows, and the beat-indexed wall ledger accumulates. It supplies temporal evidence for observing and revising a later configuration, but all outcome-affecting configuration edits occur before the film and the film removes those controls; it is not a common expiring-action process.

pre_run.reason: For every generated instance, the generator constructs solution_cells and sets target_events to the visible simulation of those cells. A successful pre-run sequence can configure those cells, start the film, send no outcome-affecting action until the 11-beat film ends, and then submit administratively. The solver corroborates this action order; its private truth read is not treated as policy information.

source_evidence.claim: The frozen test requires one common D, Delta, and bounded visible window; clause iii requires a useful action opportunity to lose value from autonomous task-state evolution, and later-enabled controls do not qualify.
Difficulty 2 is the 7x7/3-arrow/4-max/11-beat/300-ms profile, full mode is direct drag plus placed-arrow clicks, and the observation bound is 600 ms with 5 frames.
The environment is a visible moving-arrow board and configures a 600 ms frame window, 5 frames, and 120 seconds of play time.
The task rules describe one-square beat motion, wall reversal, clockwise encounters, and edits before the film, with a program verifier.
The generator simulates wall events and collision turns, applies the supplied difficulty parameters, and constructs target_events from a generated solution while retaining solution_cells in truth.
Full mode records direct drag and placed-arrow click edits only through the edit phase, while the rendered UI visibly shows the target ledger, board, beat controls, and direct-placement surface.

Each beat updates positions, wall events, reversals, collision turns, and visible ledger/flash state; the film applies the first beat immediately and schedules later beats at contract.beat_ms until completion.
Manual stepping is action-triggered, and running disables or rejects editing, stepping, resetting, revising, and submission controls until the film reaches the appropriate phase.
The target and observed ledgers are visible, and wall rails visibly flash on wall hits; the other timed visual effects are presentation state.
Authoritative grading replays the submitted starting cells for the requested beats and compares the resulting wall-event sequence; it does not require an action during the film.
The solver configures all solution cells before clicking Run, waits for complete, and submits afterward, corroborating a pre-run solution chronology.

The shared clock queues timers while paused and advances them only during running windows, so the 300 ms film is the autonomous task-time process in live mode and fixed observation windows in paused mode.
The task verifier loads the independent collision-chimes grader and validates the exported result after the UI run.
The verifier helper only loads the exported result; it does not introduce an additional outcome-affecting interaction during the film.
